title: Adaptive micro-batch thresholds with hysteresis and preemptive KV eviction for high QPS
creator: Alana Soto
description:
Problem: under sustained high QPS we see oscillation between large micro-batches (good throughput) and aggressive backpressure/eviction (avoids OOM) which causes tail-latency spikes and repeated cache thrash. Goal: implement an adaptive micro-batch cap that reacts to request inter-arrival patterns and SLO headroom using hysteresis to prevent flip-flopping, and couple this with a preemptive, score-driven KV eviction strategy plus lightweight GPU memory compaction to reduce fragmentation.

Design summary:
- Dynamic batch caps: compute per-worker soft_cap and hard_cap. soft_cap targets sustained median latency < SLO (configurable per-route). hard_cap is a safety ceiling derived from measured peak-kv-usage and free GPU memory. Caps update on a moving window of request inter-arrival rates (p95 arrival rate) and recent token throughput. Changes require a sustained deviation (hysteresis window) of N seconds to apply so we avoid oscillation.
- Hysteresis and smoothing: apply exponential smoothing to arrival-rate estimate and enforce hysteresis windows for increasing vs decreasing caps (longer window when increasing to be conservative).
- KV eviction policy: maintain a lightweight token-priority score per prefix using a decayed hit counter + reservoir-sampled recent contribution. Eviction is preemptive: if GPU memory used > soft_mem_threshold (e.g., 70%), asynchronously evict lowest-score prefixes until usage < soft_mem_target. If usage exceeds hard_mem_threshold (e.g., 92%), trigger synchronous emergency eviction and reduce soft_cap to min(soft_cap/2, base_cap).
- Prefetch protection: entries referenced by in-flight requests are protected (soft pin) to avoid evicting required KV during generation.
- GPU fragmentation & compaction: expose gpu_frag_pct metric (free_vs_largest_block) via CUDA allocator hooks. If fragmentation > 15% and free pool < X, schedule background compaction that attempts to consolidate free blocks via a short-lived buffer reallocation pattern (best-effort, non-blocking).
- Fallthrough: if eviction + compaction fail to free enough memory, apply per-request preemption (flush oldest micro-batch and resume) and route overflow to a lower-capacity model variant to keep tail latency bounded.

Implementation plan:
1) Simulation harness (local) to replay production arrival traces and KV access traces (collect traces from staging for last 7 days). 2 weeks.
2) Implement dynamic-cap controller in runtime: arrival estimator, hysteresis state machine, per-worker soft/hard caps (feature flag gated). 2 weeks.
3) Integrate KV eviction scoring into cache manager: reservoir sampling for recency component, decayed hit counter, async eviction worker with rate limiter. 2 weeks.
4) Add CUDA allocator probes for fragmentation metric and naive compaction routine (best-effort). 1 week.
5) Canary rollout: internal canary on dedicated pool with synthetic high-QPS traffic and real customer traffic shadowing. Gradual ramp, monitor gpu_mem_used, gpu_frag_pct, p99 latency, error rate. Rollback on >20% p99 regression or any OOM. 1 week.

Acceptance criteria:
- On synthetic high-QPS replay, p99 tail latency reduced by >=25% vs baseline oscillatory behavior and throughput degradation during sustained bursts.
- No increase in OOM incidents in canary.
- KV cache hit-rate degradation <= 5% compared to baseline (measured at steady-state), and eviction churn reduced vs current aggressive approach.
- Metrics added: dynamic_cap{worker}, soft_mem_threshold, hard_mem_threshold, gpu_frag_pct, kv_evicted_count, eviction_latency_ms.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Evicting low-score prefixes may increase downstream token compute if those prefixes return to hot. Hysteresis aims to mitigate.
- Compaction increases short-lived allocations; must ensure compaction is rate-limited to avoid pressure.
- Complexity: controller state must be resilient across worker restarts; persist minimal state in shared store for cross-worker coordination if needed.

Rollout notes: feature-flag default OFF. Start with simulation, then internal canary, then small customer canary (dedicated pools), then global enable with config defaults conservative.
